findings.claim: The indexed Tauri macOS guide explicitly warns that GUI apps do not inherit PATH from shell dotfiles.
findings.applicability: Relevant environment/discovery exception for launcher proof; cannot assume an interactive-shell PATH is the GUI environment.
findings.limits: This is a source observation, not a choice to adopt Tauri, its suggested fix-path-env crate, a shell, or any dependency installation.

findings.claim: Official Tauri docs describe macOS application bundles and Windows installer formats as concrete platform artifacts with packaging steps and constraints.
findings.applicability: Supports precise naming of the deliverable and distinguishing platform packaging examples from a relocatable source/app folder. Mac success or cross-compilation output alone does not establish this project's native Windows execution.
findings.exceptions: Tauri notes NSIS cross-compilation is possible with caveats while WiX MSI creation requires Windows; Microsoft WAP platform compatibility is specific to that build workflow.
findings.limits: These are examples, not proof that every Windows program requires an installer or that a plain folder cannot run. Native parity must be independently demonstrated under the root contract.

findings.claim: Tauri Windows installer documentation distinguishes runtime download, embedding and omission; skipping an absent required WebView2 runtime leaves the app unable to run.
findings.applicability: Illustrates why external versus included runtime dependencies must be explicit in packaging proof and tested for availability.
findings.limits: No selected text establishes Python or native PDF renderer discovery, versions, bundling, licensing or installation rules. WebView2 is a Tauri-specific example and is not being added as a project dependency.

findings.claim: The Windows guide includes an NSIS hook example with quoted installer paths, ExecWait child execution and a captured success/failure code.
findings.applicability: Concrete limited example that dependency execution has path and exit-status handling.
findings.limits: It is not Python argv-array semantics, full path-with-spaces correctness or propagation of a child status to the launcher caller. The example is NSIS syntax even though its heading says MSI Installer Example; it is not an implementation template for this task.

findings.claim: The macOS bundle guide maps custom resource sources relative to tauri.conf.json into destinations in the application bundle.
findings.applicability: Framework-specific example of explicit source/destination anchoring.
findings.limits: Does not establish generic Python current-directory independence, relocatability, packaged-file immutability or the correct location of mutable user/project data.

findings.claim: The selected sources do not establish externally installed Python/native renderer requirements or the generic launcher algorithm.
topics: Native PDF renderer discovery and ABI/dependency closure
Paths with spaces and platform quoting correctness
Child exit propagation to external caller
findings.reason: PyPA indexed text is a landing page. Related Tauri/NSIS examples do not supply these Python contracts. Root engineering contract and concrete local/native checks remain authority; unsupported does not mean disallowed.

findings.claim: Generated answer characterizes bundle Resources as read-only assets and uses an MSIX app-attach training card as support for separating mutable project data.
findings.reason: The read source bundle tree identifies Resources but gives no read-only guarantee. The MSIX text is a related Azure Virtual Desktop training description; it does not define storage separation for a custom launcher.
findings.resolution: Do not adopt either statement as the project-data policy; record that separation as an explicit local engineering requirement.

findings.claim: Generated answer overgeneralizes selected packaging options into a statement that Windows and macOS require these distinct installer binaries/layouts for generic apps.
findings.reason: The bodies describe Tauri and Visual Studio packaging workflows and their constraints, not an exhaustive requirement on all relocatable applications.
findings.resolution: No standalone installer or native parity claim follows from a source archive. Conversely, the source scope does not prohibit an explicitly dependency-requiring folder proof.
